blocks.text: *How you grow — the six base stats, and the Ring that scales your power.*
Primary stats
Six base stats you allocate as you level — **anyone can raise any of them** (there are no classes):

items: **STR** — melee attack power and how much you can carry
**DEX** — ranged attack power, accuracy and cast speed

blocks.text: **You choose your starting stats when you create a character**, by pulling the corners of a hexagon. Opposite stats — STR and INT, AGI and LUK, VIT and DEX — always add up to 10, so raising one lowers its partner, and every shape spends all your starting points. After that you get points to spend as you level, and **each point into a stat costs more the higher that stat already is** — every block of ten gets pricier. So a lopsided build is genuinely expensive: going all-in on one stat buys fewer total points than spreading out. What you can afford is fixed by your level; nothing else grants stat points.
What each point actually buys

Every stat feeds several numbers at once — that spread is what makes a build. The stat that leads an attack also grows faster the higher it goes: **STR adds (STR ÷ 10)² more melee attack, DEX adds (DEX ÷ 10)² more ranged attack**, and INT's square widens your magic attack. The exact per-point values:

rows: +1 MELEE ATK plus (STR ÷ 10)², +⅕ RANGED ATK, and +30 to how much you can carry
+1% max HP, soft DEF (VIT ÷ 2, plus the larger of VIT × 0.3 or VIT² ÷ 150 − 1), and +1 health regenerated every 6 seconds per 5 points
+1 M.ATK, the top of your magic attack rising by (INT ÷ 5)² and the bottom by (INT ÷ 7)², +1% max MP, +1 soft M.DEF, and +1 mana regenerated every 8 seconds per 6 points
+1 RANGED ATK plus (DEX ÷ 10)², +1 HIT (accuracy), +⅕ MELEE ATK, 0.1% faster attacks, steadier physical damage, and a shorter cast wind-up — reaching **instant casting at 150 DEX**

+0.3% crit chance, +0.2% crit damage, +⅕ MELEE ATK and RANGED ATK, and **perfect dodge**: 0.1% of ordinary attacks miss you outright, even critical ones. It works defensively against crits too: every point of your LUK lowers an attacker's crit chance against you by 0.2%

blocks.text: **Nothing in combat can change these six.** No buff, debuff, potion or ailment touches a primary stat — they come from your points and your gear alone. What skills move instead is the list below.
Every number on your sheet, and what feeds it
These are the numbers combat actually reads. A buff or debuff can move any of them for a while; your primaries and your gear set where they sit at rest.

rows: STR + (STR ÷ 10)², DEX ÷ 5, LUK ÷ 5, your level, your gear, the Attack ring stat — what normal attacks and physical skills use while you hold anything that isn't a bow or sniper rifle (and a shuriken while your STR is at least your DEX), or nothing at all

DEX + (DEX ÷ 10)², STR ÷ 5, LUK ÷ 5, your level, your gear, the *same* Attack ring stat — what normal attacks and physical skills use while you hold a bow, or a shuriken with more DEX than STR, and what a sniper rifle's physical skills use — its normal attack is a magic shot that uses your Magic Attack
INT + (INT ÷ 5)² at the top and INT + (INT ÷ 7)² at the bottom, your level, your gear, the Magic Attack ring stat

two parts. **Hard DEF** is a percentage taken off every physical hit, from your armour, the Defense lines Ink writes, the Bulwark armour word, the Defense ring stat and timed defence buffs. **Soft DEF** is a flat amount taken off after that, from VIT and your level. A critical hit ignores both
the same two parts for magic: hard M.DEF from cloth armour, Ink, Bulwark and the *same* Defense ring stat; soft M.DEF from INT and your level
a level curve raised 1% per VIT, your gear, the HP ring stat
a level curve raised 1% per INT, your gear, the MP ring stat
your level + DEX, accuracy written on your gear, the Accuracy ring stat. Your chance to hit is **HIT + 80 − your target's FLEE**, in percent — never below 5%, up to 100%
your level + AGI, evasion on your gear (Ink, and leather armour), the Evasion ring stat. **Every creature attacking you past the second takes 10% off it**, and twelve or more always hit
AGI and DEX, your gear, the Attack Speed ring stat. Shown as a number up to **190** — five attacks a second
DEX alone decides it, reaching instant at 150; the Cast Speed ring stat shortens whatever is left
1% + LUK at 0.3% a point, your gear, the Critical ring stat — it can reach 100%
starts at 200%, plus 0.2% a point of LUK, plus the *same* Critical ring stat — never above 300%
every 6 seconds, VIT ÷ 5 plus your max HP ÷ 200 (at least 1), whole numbers — paid out a little at a time
every 8 seconds, 1 plus INT ÷ 6 plus your max MP ÷ 100, whole numbers (from 120 INT, another (INT − 120) ÷ 2 + 4) — paid out a little at a time

a physical swing rolls between a floor and its maximum; the floor starts at 55% and closes as DEX rises, hitting full around 38 points. A spell rolls between the bottom and the top of your magic attack

blocks.text: Numbers your stats don't touch
A few things come from somewhere other than your six stats. They're real numbers that matter in a fight — they just aren't bought with points.

rows: your character's own speed, multiplied by whatever is slowing or hastening you — never above 250%
none from gear — only the Fist's defence skills block *(coming with its skills)*
none from gear — a skill can add jumps to your thrown shuriken and your bouncing skills for a while *(coming with its skills)*
Neutral, unless an Armor Converter is running — then its element, at level 1. Incoming attacks are scaled against it
a flat pool of 100. Sprinting drains 25 a second; it refills at 30 standing still, 18 walking, and 8 doing anything else
0 at rest — they exist only while gear or a skill grants them. Life steal returns at most 25% of a hit, reflect sends back at most 50%

blocks.text: How regeneration works

HP and MP both tick back up on their own, several times a second, and the fraction is never lost — a rate too small to pay a whole point this tick is carried to the next, so 0.3 a second really is 0.3 a second.
A debuff can **stop** your regeneration but can never reverse it. Push a regen rate below zero and it simply pays nothing — it will not drain you, and it will not heal an enemy you cast it on.

Any time your HP goes up — a potion, a heal, natural regeneration, anything added later — you'll see the same **green number** float over your head. Monsters get it too, so you can always see when something is healing itself.
The Ring — your growth engine

The Ring is a **closed loop of ten percentage-based passive stats** that you build up as you level. It is part of your character — nothing to wear, nothing to lose — and a separate layer from your weapons: **a weapon's mastery points buy your skills**, and the **Ring scales their power**. Your progress on the Ring is saved with your character.
The ten Ring stats
Going clockwise around the loop:
**Defense → HP → Attack → Accuracy → Cast Speed → Magic Attack → MP → Evasion → Critical → Attack Speed →** *(back to Defense)*

The two **poles sit dead-opposite: Defense (top) and Magic Attack (bottom)**, with the survival stats bridging them — so drifting from a physical toward a magic build naturally carries you across the defenses in between.
Two stats do double duty: **Defense** raises both your physical *and* magic defense (there is no separate magic-defense stat), and **Critical** raises both your crit rate *and* your crit damage.
The draft — a steering wheel
Every level-up you pick **one of four** options:

items: **Three known** — your current stat plus its **two neighbors** on the ring (a sliding window of three).
**One wildcard** — a random stat from elsewhere on the ring.

blocks.text: Picking the center keeps stacking that stat; picking a neighbor slides your window that way; the wildcard jumps you across the ring.
Ranks, and where the Ring stops

Every Ring stat gives a **percentage**, not flat points, so it never goes obsolete as your gear grows: **each rank is worth +1%**, and a stat takes **at most 33 ranks** (+33%). The one exception is **Defense, where each rank is +1 hard DEF** against both physical and magic hits. The Ring itself levels up to **99**, which is **99 points — enough to fill three stats completely**. Which three is your build.
Your Ring locks your role

**Most of a skill's power is your Ring** — and that scaling is role-bound: **healing scales off MP**, **damage scales off Attack / Magic Attack**. So a support who invested MP hits like wet paper with a damage weapon, and a damage build heals for crumbs with a staff. A skill's own level adds to that (see *Skills*), but the weight of it stays bound to the stats you chose. **Changing weapons changes which skills you may use — never the stats behind them.**
*(Ring upgrades that add whole new behaviors from investment are a planned future addition — for now the Ring only scales numbers.)*
Monsters use this exact system

Everything on this page describes **monsters too**. They have the same six stats, the same formulas behind them, the same rising cost per point, and the same level-based budget — a level 20 monster carries what a level 20 player could have bought. They wear real equipment, and a monster can carry Ring investment of its own, by the same ranks and the same 33-rank limit.
There is no difficulty multiplier anywhere. A monster is hard because of its level, its stats, and its gear — the same three things that make you hard. See *Monsters*.
Every kind of power has a limit

**Everything that makes you stronger stops somewhere.** Your level, every stat, the Ring, every grade and fold, every Ink line and card slot — each has a ceiling. Nothing grows forever just because you played longer, so **a player who starts today can always reach exactly where a veteran stands**. What separates players is the build they chose and how they play it, never the hours they put in.

rows: 90% of a hit, from every source together

blocks.text: **Some limits are easy to reach, some are not.** Comfort stats like attack speed and cast speed reach their limit with good gear well before the best gear exists. The ones that make you nearly untouchable — hard defence and dodging — take the best gear and a full Ring. Your character sheet shows each limit beside its number, so you can always see when more of something stops helping and your points are better spent elsewhere.

**Reaching the top is the start of a different game, not the end of one.** Every weapon has its own skills and mastery, every Ring stat combination plays differently, and the strongest elites and the shadows are called by summoning — with materials only other elites drop. Once your numbers are capped, there's always another build to master, another boss to call, another corner of the world to explore.
Reading your character sheet
Press **C** to open your character sheet. It lists every number that decides how you fight, and it updates **live** — buffs and debuffs appear the moment they land and vanish when they run out.
The big number is always **your own stat**. Anything a buff or debuff is doing to it sits in **parentheses** right after it:

items: **Green** — something is helping you, e.g. `MELEE ATK 120-140 (+24)`
**Red** — something is hurting you, e.g. `HIT 82 (-30)` while blinded
**No parentheses** — nothing is affecting that stat right now

blocks.text: The sheet reads from the same numbers combat does, so what you see is exactly what you hit for — never an estimate.
What you'll find on it:

rows: MELEE ATK · RANGED ATK · M.ATK · CRIT chance and crit damage · HIT
DEF and M.DEF (hard % + soft, with the 90% limit beside them) · FLEE · GUARD (defence a buff is adding) · BARRIER
ASPD (attack speed, with the 190 limit beside it) · CAST (between casts) · WIND-UP (cast time) · MOVE and RUN speed
LEECH (HP from damage) · MP LEECH · REFLECT
